manufacture: LOD2 and LOD3 remain simplified representations of the same manufactured crescent latch, not broad rectangular substitutes. The operating lever remains one continuous swept metal body; plate and keeper remain separate physical masses before being combined into one renderer per LOD. This preserves product identity while reducing arc-ring density for realtime distance rendering.
dimensionsThickness: LOD0, LOD1, LOD2 and LOD3 share a 34 mm lever centerline radius, 130 degree sweep, 10 x 10 mm lever section and 2 mm corner break. LOD2 uses 8 arc rings and LOD3 uses 5. Both retain the 30 x 80 x 8 mm plate and 24 x 66 x 10 mm simplified keeper envelope used by LOD1 so the object does not collapse into a different silhouette at the far transitions.
materialsFinish: LOD2 and LOD3 continue to use the canonical aged sash-metal material from the parent assembly. Metallic response, roughness, oxidation, contact polish, Fresnel response and micro-scratches remain material or lighting behavior. No painted highlight, emission, chrome-like substitute, baked reflection stripe or LOD-specific material swap is permitted.
mounting: All far proxies stay in the original per-window LODGroup and local sash-latch coordinate system. Base plate, swept lever and keeper are combined into one render mesh for each far LOD; no gameplay collider, floating helper geometry or independent transform is introduced.
interfacesGapsSeals: The far proxies preserve the same meeting-stile, pivot and receiver relationship as LOD1 and remain outside the optical glass and glazing-gasket envelope. Simplification may remove sub-pixel fasteners and pivot relief, but it may not broaden into a slab, bridge the keeper gap, penetrate the sash or materially change visible lever reach.
orientationExposure: Sheltered vertical sash hardware under the same coherent midsummer Japanese sun, sky fill, contact/occlusion and reflection-probe state as near LODs. Far transitions are most sensitive to silhouette width, specular centroid and cross-fade shimmer in oblique or grazing motion.
aging: No new far-LOD weathering layer is introduced. The proxy inherits the parent aged-metal material and therefore cannot add independent rust, wetness, dirt, value shifts or highlight stripes when switching LOD.
geometryVsMaterial: Crescent centerline, sweep, section, corner break, plate/keeper volume and LOD decimation are geometry. Fine oxidation, extrusion character, micro-scratches, roughness, contact polish, wetness and Fresnel response remain material/lighting properties. Distance simplification reduces arc rings rather than replacing the physical curve with texture or painted shading.
lodPolicy: LOD0 uses 32 crescent arc rings, LOD1 16, LOD2 8 and LOD3 5 while preserving the same physical envelope. Parent screen-relative thresholds remain 0.0060, 0.0030, 0.0012 and 0.0004 with animated cross-fade. Eight deterministic 11 mm metric-UV phase variants are retained at every far LOD. Any visible silhouette snap, specular-centroid jump, phase discontinuity, shimmer or LOD pop remains a critical failure until disproved by actual 4K temporal evidence.
weatheringCausality: Cause-based aging remains inherited from the parent material/exposure model. This refinement changes manufactured form and temporal continuity only; it does not invent source-independent dirt, wetness, rust or damage.
lookdevBrief: Native 4K temporal oblique: drive each latch through 0.003 and 0.0012 transitions and reject any perceivable crescent-to-slab change, width jump, highlight snap or shimmer. Grazing motion: track the highlight centroid from 16 to 8 to 5 rings; it may simplify but must not jump direction or become a rectangular stripe. Forced-LOD 100-percent crop: compare lever reach, keeper clearance, plate envelope and UV phase across LOD1/2/3. Static hero scoring remains based only on actual rendered pixels, never this implementation contract.
